resources.string: Sign from CodexCloud using keys on this phone

Connect this app to Tailscale without a system VPN. Assuan uses tailnet port 17373 and gpg-bridge uses 17389. A blank node list allows every Tailscale node; a filled list restricts access. Choose individual local signing keys or select all. Signatures require approval here unless you enable automatic approval for gpg-bridge Git signatures. Android 7 or later is required.
Control server HTTPS URL (blank for Tailscale)
Allowed stable node IDs (comma separated; blank allows all)
Agent active. Tap to see login and connection status.
Key passphrase (blank for an unprotected key)

Keep this key’s passphrase in phone memory for the current connection. Approval screens fill it in automatically; you can edit it and must still approve each signature. Disconnecting clears it. A blank value clears this key’s prefill.
Connect first. Prefilled passphrases last only for the current connection.

Connect and sign in to Tailscale, select signing keys and configure allowed peers first. Then retry.

Paste this credential into gpg-bridge connect on your authorized cloud node. It stays valid, including across restarts of the phone, until you revoke it here. Keep the connection string out of logs and source control.

gpg-bridge active on tailnet port 17389; the connection string stays valid until revoked
gpg-bridge connection string saved; it resumes when Tailscale is connected
Automatically approve gpg-bridge Git commit and tag signatures

Git commits and tags requested through gpg-bridge will be signed without asking, using a saved passphrase (or none for an unprotected key). Anyone holding the connection string who can reach this phone through an allowed tailnet node can then sign in your name until you revoke it. Assuan requests still require a tap. A notification is shown after each automatic signature.
Start remote signing after the phone boots
Save key passphrase on this device

Stored encrypted with a non-exportable Android Keystore key. It fills in approval screens and is used for automatic gpg-bridge signing. It survives restarts and is deleted when the app data is cleared. The passphrase is checked before saving.
Saving the passphrase failed. See the diagnostic log.
